newsitem.title: FRANCE: Central African leader meets ailing Zaire president.
newsitem.headline: Central African leader meets ailing Zaire president.

text.p: The President of the Central African Republic met his ailing "big brother" Zaire President Mobutu Sese Seko on Saturday but insisted they had not talked politics.

After an hour of talks with Mobutu, who is convalescing on the French Riviera after cancer surgery in August, President Ange Felix Patasse told reporters he had not "come to raise political issues" such as the refugee crisis in the Great Lakes.
Asked about plans to despatch a multinational force after a Rwandan-backed rebellion now controlling large areas of eastern Zaire, Patasse answered:

"I have come here to bring my moral support to the president...I don't want to bring him more worries. We have avoided tackling political problems, that's the truth," Patasse said, referring to Mobutu as his "big brother".
Asked about a revolt in the Central African Republic by mutinous soldiers, Patasse said "I believe that on the national level, the people are behind me."
Mobutu arrived in France from Switzerland on November 4 planning to stay for several weeks and has held a string of consultations on the Zaire crisis at his villa at Roquebrune-Cap-Martin near Nice.
Since arriving in France, Mobutu has also met his Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo, U.N. envoy Raymond Chretien, Congo President Pascal Lissouba and Gabonese President Omar Bongo.
